page: Microsoft Azure E4ns_v6 is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the Env6 family. It is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The instance features 4 vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, resulting in 2 threads per core. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The processor features a large 260 MB L3 cache, alongside 2 MB L2 and 48 KB L1d caches. There is no local storage bundled with this instance, though it is Premium Storage capable, and it does not include any GPU hardware.

Benchmark data indicates a divergence between single-core and multi-core performance. The single-core CPU performance, measured via stress-ng at 1916.18, is in the average tier, while multi-core performance drops to the weak tier at 3927.87. Memory bandwidth tests show weak performance, with read-only large block speeds at 31.34 GB/sec and write large block speeds at 23.07 GB/sec. However, single-threaded gzip compression is a notable strength, achieving 31.08 GB/sec. Passmark CPU and memory scores sit in the average range, but database operations and Redis SET operations perform weakly. For lightweight machine learning, the instance handles prompt processing for a small 135M LLM model at an average speed of 472.46 tokens per second.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the E4ns_v6 offers a dense memory allocation relative to its vCPU count, making it suitable for workloads that require more RAM than raw compute power. However, the tradeoff lies in its weaker multi-core scaling and lower memory bandwidth, which may limit its effectiveness for heavy parallel processing or high-throughput database operations. This instance is best suited for network-optimized tasks, static web serving, single-threaded compression jobs, and memory-bound applications that do not require high-performance local NVMe storage.
